_comment: Spec 14 §2's `memory-quality` gate thresholds (open question O2/O3's memory-router half; spec 08 §7's `[OPEN]` target P/R), consumed by `crates/xtask/src/memory_bench/gate.rs`. Versioned deliberately: a retune is a reviewable diff with a stated justification, never an edited literal in code (mirrors T12-05's search-gate precedent).
derivation: Re-derived (T14-07 Phase 7) after the default model changed to gemma-4-e2b-it-gguf-q4-0 (ADR-0006, second round -- requested directly by the user after the first round already shipped). The shipped default's real baseline run (fixtures/memory/baseline/run-gemma-4-e2b.json): precision=0.6667, recall=0.6364, f1=0.6512, exact_match_rate=0.6190 on all 42 memory.router.op.* cases, using a chat_template_override ("gemma", the older Gemma 1-3 template convention -- see ADR-0006's Consequences for why the runtime does not recognize Gemma 4's own native template; T14-09 tracks generalizing this). These floors sit a real margin below the measured run (precision -0.067, recall -0.086) -- wider than the first round's ~0.02-0.03 margin, deliberately, because this run used a template-override path (system message merged into the user turn) rather than the model's own designed template, so the margin also absorbs some of that uncertainty, not only cross-host Metal/BLAS numeric variance under deterministic greedy decoding. A materially worse run must still fail. The first round's real, measured numbers (qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-gguf-q4km: precision=0.3784/recall=0.3182; qwen2.5-1.5b-instruct-gguf-q4km: precision=0.3659/recall=0.3409) are kept on disk (fixtures/memory/baseline/run.json, run-1.5b.json) as real prior evidence, not deleted, per this project's 'do not rewrite prior progress evidence' rule -- they are simply superseded as the *current* baseline. Raising these floors further is future work (T14-09's generalized templating may unlock Gemma 4's native system-role template and a higher real ceiling, plus better prompting/more fixture coverage); lowering them requires a new measured regression, documented here.
